## Intuición: 2 de la función inversa {.title-line}

```{python}
#| echo: false
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatch

def _hd_out(ax, cx, cy, r=0.48):
    ax.add_patch(mpatch.Circle((cx, cy), r, fill=False,
                               ec='#4169E1', lw=3, zorder=3))

def _hd_cap(ax, cx, cy, r=0.48):
    ax.add_patch(mpatch.Circle((cx, cy), r, fc='#2255cc',
                               ec='#4169E1', lw=2, zorder=3))
    ax.add_patch(mpatch.FancyBboxPatch(
        (cx - r*0.85, cy + r*0.62), r*1.7, r*0.32,
        boxstyle='round,pad=0.02', fc='#112299',
        ec='#112299', zorder=4))

def _arr2(ax, x1, y1, x2, y2, lbl=''):
    ann = ax.annotate('', xy=(x2, y2), xytext=(x1, y1),
                      arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-|>', color='#4169E1',
                                     lw=3, mutation_scale=30))
    ann.arrow_patch.set_zorder(10)
    if lbl:
        ax.text((x1+x2)/2, (y1+y2)/2 + 0.28, f'${lbl}$',
                ha='center', va='center', fontsize=15,
                color='#666', style='italic')

def _inv2(d, m):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.0, 4.5))
    fig.patch.set_facecolor('white'); ax.set_facecolor('white')
    ax.set_xlim(0, 8); ax.set_ylim(0, 4.5); ax.axis('off')
    dy, r = 3.2, 0.52
    dx1, dx2, dx3 = 1.0, 3.8, 6.6
    my = 1.35
    mx1, mx2, mx3 = 1.0, 3.8, 6.6
    tk = dict(ha='center', va='center', fontsize=28,
              color='#555', style='italic', weight='bold')
    # === DIAGRAM ===
    if d >= 1:
        _hd_out(ax, dx1, dy, r)
    if d >= 2:
        _arr2(ax, dx1+r+0.08, dy, dx2-r-0.08, dy, 'f')
        _hd_cap(ax, dx2, dy, r)
    if d >= 3:
        _arr2(ax, dx2+r+0.08, dy, dx3-r-0.08, dy, 'g')
        if d == 3:
            _hd_cap(ax, dx3, dy, r)
        else:
            _hd_out(ax, dx3, dy, r)
    # === MATH ROW ===
    if m >= 1:
        ax.text(mx1, my, '$x$', **tk)
    if m >= 2:
        _arr2(ax, mx1+0.42, my, mx2-0.58, my, 'f')
        ax.text(mx2, my, '$x^2$', **tk)
    if m >= 3:
        _arr2(ax, mx2+0.62, my, mx3-0.42, my, 'g')
        ax.text(mx3, my, '$x$', **tk)
    if m >= 4:
        lx = (mx1 + mx2) / 2
        ax.text(lx, my - 0.42, '$f(x)$', ha='center', va='top',
                fontsize=12, color='#888')
        ax.text(lx, my - 0.78, '$x^2$', ha='center', va='top',
                fontsize=12, color='#888')
    if m >= 5:
        lx2 = (mx2 + mx3) / 2
        ax.text(lx2, my - 0.42, '$g(x)$', ha='center', va='top',
                fontsize=12, color='#888')
        ax.text(lx2, my - 0.78, r'$\sqrt{x}$', ha='center', va='top',
                fontsize=12, color='#888')
    plt.tight_layout(pad=0.2)
    plt.show()
```

- [Qué significa que una función sea «par» o «impar».]{style="color:#c0392b; font-weight:bold;"}

```{python}
#| echo: false
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def _sym_plots():
    x = np.linspace(-2.5, 2.5, 300)
    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.5, 10.5),
                                    gridspec_kw={'hspace': 0.55})
    fig.patch.set_facecolor('white')
    for ax in (ax1, ax2):
        ax.set_facecolor('white')
        for sp in ax.spines.values():
            sp.set_visible(False)
        ax.tick_params(left=False, labelleft=False, bottom=False)
        ax.axhline(0, color='black', lw=1.2)
        ax.axvline(0, color='black', lw=1.2)
    ax1.plot(x, x**2, color='#B8860B', lw=2.5)
    ax1.set_xlim(-2.5, 2.5); ax1.set_ylim(-0.5, 7.0)
    ax1.set_xticks([0]); ax1.tick_params(labelbottom=True, labelsize=11)
    ax2.plot(x, x**3 - 4*x, color='#B8860B', lw=2.5)
    ax2.set_xlim(-2.5, 2.5); ax2.set_ylim(-6.5, 6.5)
    ax2.set_xticks([0]); ax2.tick_params(labelbottom=True, labelsize=11)
    plt.tight_layout(pad=0.4)
    plt.show()
```

${\color{goldenrod}f}({\color{teal}x}) = {\color{teal}x}^2$

::: {.fragment .fade-in data-fragment-index=1}
${\color{goldenrod}f}({\color{maroon}-x}) = ({\color{maroon}-x})^2 = {\color{teal}x}^2$
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in data-fragment-index=2}
${\color{goldenrod}f}({\color{maroon}-x}) = {\color{goldenrod}f}({\color{teal}x})$
:::

::: {style="margin-top:0.5em; display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:center; gap:0.35em;"}

${\color{goldenrod}f}({\color{teal}x}) = {\color{teal}x}^3 - 4{\color{teal}x}$


::: {.fragment .fade-in data-fragment-index=3}
${\color{goldenrod}f}({\color{maroon}-x}) = ({\color{maroon}-x})^3 - 4({\color{maroon}-x})$
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in data-fragment-index=4}
$= -{\color{teal}x}^3 + 4{\color{teal}x}$
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in data-fragment-index=5}
$= -({\color{teal}x}^3 - 4{\color{teal}x})$
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in data-fragment-index=6}
${\color{goldenrod}f}({\color{maroon}-x}) = -{\color{goldenrod}f}({\color{teal}x})$
:::

${\color{goldenrod}f}({\color{maroon}-\pi/3}) = -\sqrt{3}/2$

## Árbol de funciones simétricas {.title-line}

```{python}
#| echo: false
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatch

def _sym_tree():
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.5, 6.8))
    fig.patch.set_facecolor('white'); ax.set_facecolor('white')
    ax.set_xlim(0, 9.5); ax.set_ylim(0, 7.2); ax.axis('off')

    _CG = '#B8860B'
    _CN = '#1a237e'
    _CR = '#c0392b'
    _CT = '#17a589'

    def box(cx, cy, w, h, color, text, fs=19):
        ax.add_patch(mpatch.FancyBboxPatch(
            (cx-w/2, cy-h/2), w, h,
            boxstyle='round,pad=0.12', fill=False,
            edgecolor=color, linewidth=2.5, linestyle='--', zorder=3))
        ax.text(cx, cy, text, ha='center', va='center',
                fontsize=fs, color=color, fontweight='bold', zorder=4)

    def tree(x_top, y_top, y_branch, children, color, lw=2.3):
        ax.plot([x_top, x_top], [y_top, y_branch],
                color=color, lw=lw, zorder=2, solid_capstyle='butt')
        xs = [c[0] for c in children]
        ax.plot([min(xs), max(xs)], [y_branch, y_branch],
                color=color, lw=lw, zorder=2)
        for cx, cy_top in children:
            ax.plot([cx, cx], [y_branch, cy_top + 0.18],
                    color=color, lw=lw, zorder=2, solid_capstyle='butt')
            ax.annotate('', xy=(cx, cy_top), xytext=(cx, cy_top + 0.18),
                        arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-|>', color=color,
                                       lw=lw, mutation_scale=18))

    # Nodos
    f_cx, f_cy, f_h = 4.75, 6.0, 0.78
    s_cx, s_cy, s_h = 2.4, 3.9, 0.78
    n_cx, n_cy, n_h = 7.3, 3.9, 0.78
    p_cx, p_cy, p_h = 1.4, 1.7, 0.68
    i_cx, i_cy, i_h = 3.4, 1.7, 0.68

    box(f_cx, f_cy, 2.6, f_h, _CG, 'Función', 20)
    box(s_cx, s_cy, 2.8, s_h, _CN, 'Simétrica', 19)
    box(n_cx, n_cy, 3.2, n_h, _CR, 'No simétrica', 18)
    box(p_cx, p_cy, 1.8, p_h, _CT, 'Par', 18)
    box(i_cx, i_cy, 1.8, p_h, _CT, 'Impar', 18)

    # Conexiones
    tree(f_cx, f_cy - f_h/2, 4.55,
         [(s_cx, s_cy + s_h/2), (n_cx, n_cy + n_h/2)], _CG)
    tree(s_cx, s_cy - s_h/2, 2.8,
         [(p_cx, p_cy + p_h/2), (i_cx, i_cy + i_h/2)], _CN)

    plt.tight_layout(pad=0.2)
    plt.show()
```

```{python}

_sym_tree()
```

## Determinando la simetría usando la geometría {.title-line}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| results: 'hide'
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

def _setup_ax(ax, xlim=(-5, 5)):
    ax.set_xlim(xlim)
    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['left'].set_position(('data', 0))
    ax.spines['bottom'].set_position(('data', 0))
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)

def _draw_symmetry_even(ax, y_pos, arrow_y):
    """Dibuja línea vertical punteada y flecha horizontal roja para simetría par"""
    ax.axvline(x=0, color='#c0392b', linestyle='--', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)
    ax.annotate('', xy=(-2.5, arrow_y), xytext=(2.5, arrow_y),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='<->', color='#8b0000', lw=3))

def _draw_symmetry_odd(ax, y_pos, arrow_y):
    """Dibuja línea vertical punteada, flecha horizontal roja y flecha vertical azul para simetría impar"""
    ax.axvline(x=0, color='#c0392b', linestyle='--', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)
    ax.axhline(y=0, color='#2e8b57', linestyle='--', linewidth=1, alpha=0.7)
    ax.annotate('', xy=(-2.5, arrow_y), xytext=(2.5, arrow_y),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='<->', color='#8b0000', lw=3))
    ax.annotate('', xy=(0, -y_pos*0.8), xytext=(0, y_pos*0.8),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='<->', color='#1f5f8b', lw=3))

x = np.linspace(-5, 5, 400)
```

```{python}
ax.set_title(r'$y = x^2$', color='#b8a642', fontsize=10)
```

## ¿A quién le importa la simetría? {.title-line}

::: {style="display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex: 1; min-height: 0; padding: 0.5em 2em; gap: 1em; font-size: 1.45em; padding-right: 3em; text-align: center;font-weight: bold;"}

::: {.fragment .fade-in data-fragment-index=1 style="color: #b8a642; max-width: 80%;"}
Las funciones pares e impares tienen propiedades especiales que son relevantes para derivadas e integrales.
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in data-fragment-index=2 style="color: #8b4513; max-width: 80%;"}
También son útiles para graficar y comprender el comportamiento de las funciones.
:::

:::

## Descomponiendo la simetría {.title-line}


::: {style="display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex: 1; min-height: 0; padding: 0.5em 2em; gap: 1.5em; font-size: 1.45em; padding-right: 3em; text-align: center;"}

$$\displaystyle {\color{goldenrod}f}({\color{teal}x}) = \frac{{\color{goldenrod}f}_{\color{goldenrod}e}({\color{teal}x}) + {\color{goldenrod}f}_{\color{goldenrod}e}({\color{teal}-x})}{2} + \frac{{\color{goldenrod}f}_{\color{maroon}o}({\color{teal}x}) - {\color{goldenrod}f}_{\color{maroon}o}({\color{teal}-x})}{2}$$

::: {.fragment .fade-in data-fragment-index=1 style="color: navy; font-size: 1.45em; font-style: italic; max-width: 85%;"}
Toda función puede expresarse como la suma de una función par y una función impar.
:::

:::
